pr_title: `listDirectoriesInDirectory` fix -- check if symlinks point to directories
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/8354: inotify treats symlinks to individual files as directories.

Demo video of the fix: https://www.loom.com/share/c7044edec1ff47158fd93f49a1b0af63

issue_context.title: When directories are monitored recursively symlink targets are considered directories.
issue_context.body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to osquery! -->

# Bug report
When monitoring a directory recursively via inotify osquery struggles to deal with symlinks. This has become apparent when we tried monitoring **/etc** via **/etc/%%**. The logs got flooded with _"Could not add inotify watch on:"_ warnings.

**Notice the trailing slash as the end of the paths.** 
 
```
W0617 09:01:07.094503 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-http-image-filter.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094547 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-http-xslt-filter.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094583 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-mail.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094619 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-stream-geoip2.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094655 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-http-geoip2.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094691 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/nginx/modules-available/mod-stream.conf/
W0617 09:01:07.094780 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /etc/nginx/sites-available/default/
W0617 09:01:07.094875 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/Security_Communication_RootCA3.crt/
W0617 09:01:07.094907 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/E-Tugra_Global_Root_CA_RSA_v3.crt/
W0617 09:01:07.094949 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/GlobalSign_Root_CA_-_R6.crt/
W0617 09:01:07.094988 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/ACCVRAIZ1.crt/
W0617 09:01:07.095028 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/GlobalSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_R5.crt/
W0617 09:01:07.095068 1324473 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /usr/share/ca-certificates/mozilla/D-TRUST_EV_Root_CA_1_2020.crt/
```
It seems there is no difference whether the targeted file is within the monitored path (below /etc in this case) or outside (like files within /usr/share)



### What operating system and version are you using?
 version = 22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)
   build = 
platform = ubuntu


### What version of osquery are you using?
version = 5.12.2

### What steps did you take to reproduce the issue?
#### Prepare a directory with a symlink
```
# pwd
/home/bob
# touch file
# ln -s file1 link1
# ls -l
total 0
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 17 10:22 file1
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 5 Jun 17 10:22 link1 -> file1
```

#### simple config
```json
{
   "options": {},
   "file_paths": {
     "homes": [
       "/home/%%"
    ]
  }
}
```
#### Find warning log
```
W0617 10:29:03.180800 1325931 inotify.cpp:371] Could not add inotify watch on: /home/bob/file1/
```

### What did you expect to see?
- Expect osquery to monitor changes of the symlink file or its target. 

### What did you see instead?
- osquery tries to monitor an non existing directory.
comments: I have the same issue with Fedora 40. Tested version 5.11.10 and 5.12.2.

review_comments: Nit: Also test with `recursive=true` (and some link on a subdirectory).
Added tests with recursive. Adding a link to subdirectory is done in other tests, so not needed here.
Same as the other comment, let's test with `recursive=true`.
Because this is a link that points to itself. It cannot be resolved canonically, so it doesn't make sense to return it as a directory.
